_readme: The curated GGPK table/column list. This file IS the contract for what our
catalog is allowed to know about.
Why curated and not 'every column in the schema': the published dat-schema is
always 'latest'. Against an older client the trailing columns of a table do not
exist, so the reader walks past the end of the row and dies with
RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView
Requesting only the columns we consume keeps the read inside the row, and
extract.py validates every name against the schema first, so a GGG rename fails
loudly at config time instead of silently producing wrong data.
Adding a column is a deliberate act: add it here, say why in 'why', and re-run.
CONSUMERS: drop Royale and [DNT] rows before keying anything on Name. They
reuse real names with different numbers - SkillGemClarityRoyale is called
'Clarity' and requires level 1 where the real one requires 10 - so an unfiltered
name-keyed dict silently takes the dead value. SkillGems also lists monster and
playtest skills that are not obtainable items. See README.md.

tables.name: BaseItemTypes
tables.why: The spine. Id is the only safe join key (ADR-0004); Name is @localized so each language folder gives the translation for the same Id.
notes: TalismanEnchants carries the 3.29 talisman semi-implicits (-> Mods -> Stats).
It is the LAST column, so it is the first thing to break against a client
older than the schema. Drop it for a lag-window dump: --drop-column BaseItemTypes.TalismanEnchants

tables.name: ItemClasses
tables.why: Class grouping + the localized class label the editor shows (CLASS_CH today).

tables.name: Tags
tables.why: Resolves BaseItemTypes.TagsKeys into readable tags.

tables.name: ArmourTypes
tables.why: Replaces the CSV's armour columns. IncreasedMovementSpeed is a genuine win - FilterBlade's CSV has no such column and the campaign boot rules need it.

tables.name: WeaponTypes
tables.why: Weapon stats. DPS is derived, not stored: avg(DamageMin, DamageMax) * 1000 / Speed.

tables.name: ShieldTypes
tables.why: Block chance, the one shield stat the other tables miss.

tables.name: ComponentAttributeRequirements
tables.why: Str/Dex/Int requirements - also how the Armour/Evasion/ES defence split is derived.

tables.name: ComponentCharges
tables.why: Flask charges.

tables.name: Mods
tables.why: Implicit + talisman-enchant resolution. Structured (stat id + min/max) beats prose for tiering.

tables.name: Stats
tables.why: Stat ids, the key into stat_descriptions.txt for human-readable implicit text.

tables.name: CurrencyItems
tables.why: Stack size + the localized use-description shown in the editor.

tables.name: Flasks
tables.why: Life/mana recovery and flask type, for the campaign flask bands.

tables.name: SkillGems
tables.why: Support-vs-active and gem colour, for the Gems categories.
notes: GemVariants is an ARRAY of GemEffects - the gem's default variant plus every
transfigured one. It is the only route from a droppable gem item to its
requirement level, its gem tags and the transfigured names, none of which are

tables.name: GemEffects
tables.why: One row per gem VARIANT. Name carries the transfigured names ('Ice Nova of Frostbolts') that BaseItemTypes does not hold at all; GemTags is the only structured 'this is an aura / a herald' signal we have, replacing hand-curated lists.
notes: Name is NOT @localized, unlike BaseItemTypes.Name - so this gives English
transfigured names but not Chinese ones.

tables.name: GemTags
tables.why: The tag vocabulary GemEffects.GemTags points at (aura, herald, support, ...).

tables.name: GrantedEffects
tables.why: The join hop between a gem variant and its per-level table.

tables.name: GrantedEffectsPerLevel
tables.why: PlayerLevelReq at Level 1 IS the gem's requirement level - the number poedb prints as 'Requires Level'. BaseItemTypes.DropLevel is a different quantity (when it starts dropping) and disagrees for every act-1 quest-reward gem: Fireball is DropLevel 5, Requires Level 1.

tables.name: Maps
tables.why: Map tier.

tables.name: Words
tables.why: Unique item NAMES live here, not in BaseItemTypes. Foreign key target for the unique tables below.
notes: Words has NO Id column - join on the foreignrow index only.

tables.name: UniqueStashLayout
tables.why: The canonical unique list (~1555 rows) plus its stash-tab category.

tables.name: UniqueStashTypes
tables.why: Names the stash-tab category (Axe / Amulet / Ring ...).

tables.name: VillageUniqueDisenchantValues
tables.why: A drop-RARITY axis for unique tiering, and RuthlessValue additionally flags Ruthless availability.
notes: NOT a market price. Only ~364 distinct values across 1526 uniques (heavily
banded), and Ashes of the Stars scores 12.20 despite being expensive.
Use it as rarity; use data/unique_base_db.json for actual value.
RuthlessValue floors to 0.90 for items unobtainable in Ruthless (unique maps),
so a high Value/RuthlessValue ratio is a usable 'irrelevant in Ruthless' flag.
Derived from the Settlers village mechanic - could go stale if GGG retires it.

tables.name: UniqueMaps
tables.why: IsDropDisabled is a real droppability flag - the only one GGPK gives us, and only for unique maps.

removed.name: Talismans
removed.why: Data/Talismans.datc64 was REMOVED in 3.29 - requesting it fails the whole run with NoFileInfoError. Its Tier column was the in-game upgrade chain anyway, never a filter tier. 3.29 talisman implicits come from BaseItemTypes.TalismanEnchants instead.

checks._why: Cheap post-export smoke tests. A schema/data skew that inserts a column mid-table shifts every later offset and yields plausible-looking garbage, which no column-name validation can catch. These assert known-true values instead.

translation_probe._why: exportTables falls back to the English file when a language folder is absent, so a bad --languages silently produces an English dump labelled zh. This asserts the value actually differs.
